in_sanskrit.name: कामाख्या
in_sanskrit.meaning: Desire or Passion personified as a goddess
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The goddess of desire or passion, the feminine manifestation of the creative force of the universe, the consort of Lord Shiva in the form of the Goddess of the Womb, the goddess of sexuality and fertility, and the presiding deity of the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam.

in_hindi.name: कामाख्या
in_hindi.long_meaning: काम का अख्यात (The known or acknowledged one of desire)

in_marathi.name: Kamakhya
in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे Goddess of Desire
in_marathi.long_meaning: Kamakhya हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। The Mother of the Universe, who embodies desire, creation, destruction and transformation.

vedic_reference.note: The goddess Kamakhya is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures including the Mahabharata, the Puranas, and the Tantras. She is considered to be the embodiment of the creative energy of the universe and the consort of Lord Shiva. The Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam, is one of the most famous temples dedicated to this goddess.
